title: Privacy policy
text:
1. Purpose of this privacy policy
The Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs (DML) Working Group at the Leibniz Centre for Agricultural Landscape Research (ZALF) is committed to protecting your personal data. This privacy policy explains what personal data may be processed when you visit this website, how it is used, and what rights you have.

title: Privacy policy
text:
2. Collection of data
Since this website is a static site hosted on GitHub Pages, we do not actively collect personal data. However, the following data may be processed by our hosting provider as part of standard operation:

Log data: Information such as IP address, browser type, operating system, referring URL, pages visited, and timestamps may be logged by GitHub Pages.
Cookies: This site does not set its own tracking cookies. GitHub may use cookies as part of providing and securing their services.

Please refer to the GitHub Privacy Statement for details on their handling of log data and cookies.

title: Privacy policy
text:
3. Use of data
We do not use personal data for analytics, marketing, or profiling. Any data processed by GitHub (e.g., server logs) is used to operate and secure the hosting platform.

title: Privacy policy
text:
4. Sharing your data
We do not sell, lease, or share personal data. GitHub, as the hosting provider, may process data according to their privacy policy.

title: Privacy policy
text:
5. Data subject rights (GDPR)
Under the GDPR, you have the following rights regarding your personal data:

Right to access (Art. 15)
Right to rectification (Art. 16)
Right to erasure (Art. 17)
Right to restriction of processing (Art. 18)
Right to object (Art. 21)
Right to data portability (Art. 20)

You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority (Art. 77).

title: Privacy policy
text:
6. Data retention
We do not retain personal data through this website. Any log data processed by GitHub is retained according to GitHub’s policies.

title: Privacy policy
text:
7. Third-party services and links
This site may link to third-party websites. We are not responsible for their privacy practices. Please review the privacy policies of those websites.

title: Privacy policy
text:
8. Security measures
This static website does not operate its own user database. GitHub Pages provides operational and platform security. See GitHub’s Security overview for more details.

title: Privacy policy
text:
9. Updates to this policy
We may update this privacy policy to reflect changes in legal requirements or website functionality. Updates will be published on this page.

title: Upcoming Quarto Workshop at iEMSs 2026
text:
We are excited to announce that the DML group will host a workshop at the International Environmental Modelling and Software Society (iEMSs) 2026 conference in Dublin over the 12-16th July.
The workshop “One Publishing Tool to Rule Them All: Quarto for Documentation, Presentations, Manuscripts and Outreach”, which is being prepared in collaboration with researchers from ETH Zurich will explore Quarto as a unified solution for academic communication. Quarto can generate multiple output formats — PDF, HTML, LaTeX, and DOCX — from a single source document while supporting executable code in Python, R, Julia, and Observable. Through short presentations and guided exercises, participants will learn to produce documentation, reproducible journal articles, presentations, outreach websites, and interactive dashboards — all from one tool.
We will make the content from both the workshop available online prior to the conference, so stay tuned for more updates!

title: DML at the FAIRagro Community Summit
text:
In March, DML working group members travelled to Frankfurt to attend the FAIRagro Community Summit. The event brought together the FAIRagro community to showcase the services and tools the consortium has been developing to advance Open and FAIR data practices in agricultural research.
FAIRagro is an NFDI consortium that has represented the agrosystems research community in Germany since 2023. With more than 30 partners, it is building a FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) research data management infrastructure — developing the tools and workflows needed to support Open Science and sustainable crop production.
The summit was a great opportunity to exchange ideas, hear about ongoing developments, and connect with others working on research data challenges in agriculture. We look forward to future collaboration with the FAIRagro consortium!

title: Design System: Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs (DML)
text:
Creative North Star: “The Living Strata”
The DML identity is built on the same idea as its logo: three stacked strata. Support is the surface layer, Integration the binding middle, Transfer the deep layer that meets the world — the working group’s three services rendered as geological bands. The whole system works outward from that metaphor. Colour comes from soil and growth (forest greens, a warm teal, a single terracotta), surfaces sit on warm paper rather than clinical white, and depth is built from soft, ink-tinted shadows that layer one stratum gently over the next. Nothing is flat, and nothing shouts.
The personality is warm, collaborative, and approachable. This is a service group’s face, not an institution’s monument — a knowledgeable colleague glad you asked, not a portal you have to decode. Editorial serif headings (DM Serif Display) give academic weight; a clean geometric sans (DM Sans) keeps the body human and legible; the paper background and rounded, lifted cards lower the barrier to “discuss your project with us.” Scientific credibility is the floor, but warmth is the differentiator.
The system explicitly rejects four neighbours it could easily be mistaken for. It is not a generic SaaS landing page (no hero-metric template, no endless identical icon cards, no buzzwords). It is not a flashy startup (no purple gradients, neon, or decorative glass — the one navbar blur and the genuine dark mode are functional). It is not a sterile government portal (the paper and the serif are the antidote to bureaucratic cold). And it is not a dense academic journal (structure and whitespace carry meaning; the concept diagram and tiered service panels do the work a wall of text would otherwise do).
Key Characteristics: - Warm paper light mode (#F5F3EE); rich teal-tinted near-black dark mode (#0F1B18). - A serif-display + geometric-sans pairing carrying academic warmth. - A three-colour strata triad (Support / Integration / Transfer) that is structural, never decorative. - Soft, ink-tinted layered depth; surfaces lift on interaction rather than sitting flat. - Two signature interactive surfaces (concept diagram, support tiers) that show the model instead of describing it. - WCAG 2.1 AA, reduced-motion aware, colour-blind safe by construction.



A palette pulled from cultivated land: forest and sage greens for growth, a deep teal for authority, a single warm terracotta as the one earth tone, all resting on warm paper. Greens dominate; terracotta is rare by design.



Deep Stratum Teal (#356259): The anchor brand colour. Primary buttons, links, active nav, headings (light mode), every teal accent and tint. Desaturated and grounded, it reads as competent without going corporate-navy.
Living Teal (#36AE6C): The brighter, more alive teal. Secondary actions, the hero eyebrow rules, and the primary brand colour in dark mode (where the deep teal would disappear).





ZALF Green (#46A84F): The parent institution’s green; the growth note in the family.
Sage Light (#9EBC83): A soft light green used for headings and link/hover accents in dark mode, where it reads warmly against the near-black.
Misty Teal-Green (#80BDBD): The lightest teal; informational accents and tertiary tinting.




The three service pillars, each owning one colour. This triad is structural: it maps service → logo layer → colour, and appears on the concept diagram, the team-card top border, and the tiered service panels. - Surface Forest (#2B5D45) — Support, the surface stratum (logo layer 1). - Integration Terracotta (#A4713D) — Integration, the deep stratum (logo layer 3). The single warm earth tone, and the only non-green in the system. - Transfer Teal (#3E7775) — Transfer, the mid stratum (logo layer 2).




Warm Paper (#F5F3EE): The light-mode body background. Not white — a warm off-white that softens the whole system. The single most identity-defining neutral.
Slate (#465555): Default body text in light mode. A green-tinted dark grey, never pure black, so it sits in the family rather than fighting it.
Ink (#1A1A1A): Reserved near-black for the heaviest text.
Forest Ink (#0F1B18): The dark-mode body background — a teal-tinted near-black, deliberately richer than flat black.
Dark Surface (#162520) / Dark Border (#1F3530): Card surfaces and borders in dark mode.
Muted Gray (#6C6C6C): Captions, dates, and metadata. (In running text, body uses Slate at full strength, not this gray — see the Legibility Rule.)
Pure White (#FFFFFF): Card and surface fills that sit on top of the paper.





Olive (#B1BE4D): Warnings only.
Brick (#C0392B, #E74C3C dark): Danger / errors only.




The Strata Rule. Support is forest, Integration is terracotta, Transfer is teal — always, everywhere, in that mapping. The triad is never reassigned for visual variety and never used decoratively; if one of these colours appears, it means its pillar.
The One Earth Tone Rule. Terracotta is the only warm non-green in the system, and it belongs to Integration. Its rarity is what makes it legible. Do not introduce a second accent earth tone “for balance.”
The Legibility Rule. Body copy is Slate (#465555) on paper, never the muted gray. Gray (#6C6C6C) is for metadata only. Light-gray body text “for elegance” is forbidden — it fails our 4.5:1 floor and reads as the institutional cold we reject.




Display Font: DM Serif Display (with Georgia, Times New Roman fallback) Body Font: DM Sans (with Segoe UI, system-ui fallback) Label/Mono Font: Segoe UI Mono (with ui-monospace, Consolas fallback)
Character: An editorial serif display paired with a clean geometric sans — a deliberate contrast-axis pairing (serif + sans), not two competing sans-serifs. The serif lends academic, considered weight to headings; the sans keeps the body readable and carries the warmth and approachability through running text. DM Serif Display ships in a single weight (400), so heading hierarchy is built from size and colour, not weight.

Identity note: DM Serif Display and DM Sans are on the greenfield reflex-reject list, but they are the brand’s committed, shipped typefaces — identity-preservation wins. Do not swap them on this surface.




Display (400, clamp(2.1rem, 5.5vw, 3.75rem), line-height 1.13, letter-spacing −0.01em): Hero headline only. Sentence case, balanced wrap. Tight, refined tracking — never wide or uppercased.
Headline (400, clamp(1.75rem, 3vw, 2.35rem), line-height 1.08): Major section titles (e.g. the support-tiers heading). Serif, teal-dark in light mode.
Title (400, 1.45rem, line-height 1.18, −0.01em): Card titles — team names, panel taglines. Serif, balanced wrap.
Body (400, 1rem, line-height 1.65): Running text in DM Sans. Generous leading. Cap measure at ~64ch (the components already constrain intros to 64ch / hero copy to 56ch).
Label (700, 0.68rem, letter-spacing 0.15em, UPPERCASE): Section eyebrows, column labels, the hero eyebrow, skill/role kickers. DM Sans, tracked, muted gray or tier colour. Short phrases only (≤4 words).
Mono (400, 0.9em): Inline code and kbd, on a paper-tinted (#EAE6DF) or dark-surface background.




The Serif-for-Voice, Sans-for-Cards Rule. Page and section headings are serif (editorial weight). But card titles in listings (news, projects) deliberately switch to DM Sans semibold near-black — the serif is reserved for identity moments, not every repeated grid title. Team-member names keep the serif because a person is an identity moment; a news headline is information.
The No-Weight-Crutch Rule. DM Serif Display has one weight. Build heading emphasis from size and colour, never from a bold that doesn’t exist. Never fake it with font-weight on the serif.




The system is softly layered, not flat. Surfaces (cards, panels, the navbar) carry a quiet resting shadow and lift toward you on hover (translateY(-3px) to -4px) with a deeper shadow. The signature detail: shadows are tinted toward Forest Ink (rgba(15, 27, 24, …)), not pure black, so depth stays inside the warm palette instead of muddying it. The navbar uses a light glass treatment — backdrop-filter: blur(12px) over rgba(255,255,255,0.95) — the one place a blur is intentional rather than decorative.



Resting card (box-shadow: 0 12px 30px rgba(15,27,24,0.08), 0 3px 8px rgba(15,27,24,0.04)): The default lift for team cards and panels. Two layers: a soft ambient spread plus a tight contact shadow.
Hover card (box-shadow: 0 18px 36px rgba(15,27,24,0.12), 0 6px 14px rgba(15,27,24,0.06)): The lifted state, paired with translateY(-4px).
Listing hover (box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.09), 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.05)): Lighter cards (news/projects) rise on hover from a flat resting state.
Button (resting 0 2px 8px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); hover 0 4px 14px rgb(53 98 89 / 0.25)): The hover shadow tints toward teal-dark, glowing in the brand colour.
Floating panel (0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.1), 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.05)): Dropdown menus and the concept-diagram panels.




The Ink-Not-Black Rule. Shadows on light surfaces tint toward Forest Ink (rgba(15, 27, 24, …)), never rgba(0,0,0,…) at full neutrality. The warmth of the paper must survive into its shadows.
The Lift-on-Intent Rule. Surfaces rest quietly and lift only in response to the user (hover, focus). Elevation is feedback, not decoration. (Reduced-motion users get the colour/shadow change without the translate — see Do’s.)







Shape: Gently rounded rectangles (8px / 0.5rem radius) — deliberately not pills (the brand moved off the 9999px pill).
Primary (.btn-brand): Deep Stratum Teal fill, white text, 600 weight, 0.65rem 1.5rem padding, a 1.5px teal border, and a soft resting shadow. Hover deepens the fill to #2A4E47 and lifts the shadow into a teal glow.
Hero / ghost (.hero-btn): On the dark hero, the same shape goes transparent with a rgba(255,255,255,0.4) border and near-white text; hover fills with rgba(255,255,255,0.1) and brightens the border. No shadow.
Button row: Buttons centre, wrap, and cap at 260px; on mobile they stack full-width.





Skill chip (.listing-skill): Pill-rounded (1rem), teal-tinted fill (rgba(teal-dark, 0.06)) with a faint teal border, teal-dark 700-weight UPPERCASE micro-label. Static (not interactive).
Project link (.project-link): 8px-rounded teal-tinted chip, semibold, deepens its tint on hover.
Category badge (.listing-category): Small 4px-rounded teal-tinted tag, 600-weight UPPERCASE, on news/project cards. Non-interactive (cursor: default).





Corner Style: Team cards 16px (1rem); listing cards 8px; signature panels 10–18px.
Team card (.card-team): White (or dark-surface) fill with a subtle top-light gradient overlay, a 4px strata-gradient top border (Support → Integration → Transfer), a circular 150px avatar inside a teal ring, serif name, tracked role kicker, skill chips, and a divider’d projects list. Lifts -4px on hover.
Listing card (news/projects): White, 8px, thin border, lifts -3px on hover. Internally reordered with flex order so meta reads: category → title → description → date.
Internal padding: Cards 1.5–1.75rem; signature panels clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 1.5rem).




The site is contact-driven, so forms are minimal — the navbar search is the main field. Inputs inherit Bootstrap/Quarto defaults, restyled to the palette: teal-dark icon glyphs, transparent backgrounds in the navbar, and a teal :focus-visible outline (2px solid, 2px offset). Any new field should follow the same pattern: light stroke, paper/white fill, teal focus ring — never a heavy box.




Navbar: Light glass — rgba(255,255,255,0.95) + blur(12px), a 1px hairline bottom border, dark glass (rgba(15,27,24,0.95)) in dark mode. Links are DM Sans 500, #4E5855, with a 4px-rounded teal-tint hover pill; active links go teal-dark 600 (sage-light in dark mode).
Language switcher: A bespoke inline EN / DE toggle (not a dropdown), the current language underlined in teal-dark, the other muted gray with a slash separator. Pinned to the navbar’s right edge on desktop.
Mobile: Collapses to a teal-stroked hamburger; nav items stack in-flow.




.col-section-label / divided-column h2: DM Sans, 0.68rem, 700, 0.15em tracking, UPPERCASE, muted gray, with a 1px rule that extends to fill the row (&::after { flex: 1; height: 1px }). This is the one deliberate, named eyebrow system — used for “NEWS”, “PROJECTS” column heads, not stamped above every section.



An interactive, paper-framed diagram (aspect-ratio: 1100/720) showing the three pillars orbiting a central “DML” label. Hovering/activating a stratum opens a white panel (badge in the tier colour, serif tagline, dotted list) with a soft fade-in. The visual argument for the whole service model — it shows the strata instead of listing them.



A three-step escalating ladder (.dml-support-tiers): three stepped panels of increasing height (12.75 → 15.75 → 18.5rem) in tier-tinted fills with a 6px coloured bottom border, effort “pips”, and an expanding detail panel. Lives in a paper-gradient, 18px-rounded, soft-shadowed container. Steps lift -4px and show a teal focus outline on keyboard focus.







Do keep the Strata Rule absolute: Support = Surface Forest (#2B5D45), Integration = Integration Terracotta (#A4713D), Transfer = Transfer Teal (#3E7775), in that mapping, everywhere.
Do pair every tier colour with a label, icon, or position — colour-blind safe is non-negotiable. The strata triad must never carry meaning by colour alone.
Do set body copy in Slate (#465555) on paper at full strength; reserve muted gray (#6C6C6C) for dates and captions only. Verify ≥4.5:1 in both themes.
Do build heading hierarchy from size and colour — DM Serif Display has one weight (400).
Do tint shadows toward Forest Ink (rgba(15, 27, 24, …)), not pure black, on light surfaces.
Do give every hover/entrance animation a prefers-reduced-motion alternative: keep the colour and shadow change, drop the translateY.
Do keep the warm paper (#F5F3EE) as the light body and Forest Ink (#0F1B18) as the dark body — these define the brand more than any accent.
Do let the signature components (concept diagram, support tiers) carry structural meaning instead of writing another paragraph.





Don’t make it look like a generic SaaS landing page: no hero-metric template (big number / small label / gradient accent), no rows of identical icon-heading-text cards, no buzzwords (streamline, empower, supercharge, leverage, seamless, world-class).
Don’t make it look like a flashy startup: no dark-mode purple gradients, no neon accents, no glassmorphism as decoration. The one navbar blur is functional; do not multiply it.
Don’t make it look like a sterile government / institutional portal: never trade the warm paper and editorial serif for cold, template-stamped white.
Don’t make it read like a dense academic journal: never ship a wall of undifferentiated text — structure with hierarchy, whitespace, and the signature components.
Don’t use background-clip: text gradient text — emphasis is weight, size, or a single solid colour.
Don’t add a coloured border-left / border-right greater than 1px as a side stripe on cards or callouts. (The team-card top gradient and the tier bottom border are intentional top/bottom accents — the banned pattern is the side stripe.)
Don’t introduce a second warm/earth accent — terracotta is the only non-green, and it belongs to Integration.
Don’t stamp the tracked uppercase eyebrow above every section. It is one named system for column labels, not a per-section reflex.
Don’t revert buttons to pills — the brand uses 8px rounded rectangles.
Don’t use light-gray body text “for elegance”; it fails contrast and reads as the institutional cold the brand rejects.

Key Characteristics: - Warm paper light mode (#F5F3EE); rich teal-tinted near-black dark mode (#0F1B18). - A serif-display + geometric-sans pairing carrying academic warmth. - A three-colour strata triad (Support / Integration / Transfer) that is structural, never decorative. - Soft, ink-tinted layered depth; surfaces lift on interaction rather than sitting flat. - Two signature interactive surfaces (concept diagram, support tiers) that show the model instead of describing it. - WCAG 2.1 AA, reduced-motion aware, colour-blind safe by construction.

title: Design System: Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs (DML)
text:
A palette pulled from cultivated land: forest and sage greens for growth, a deep teal for authority, a single warm terracotta as the one earth tone, all resting on warm paper. Greens dominate; terracotta is rare by design.



Deep Stratum Teal (#356259): The anchor brand colour. Primary buttons, links, active nav, headings (light mode), every teal accent and tint. Desaturated and grounded, it reads as competent without going corporate-navy.
Living Teal (#36AE6C): The brighter, more alive teal. Secondary actions, the hero eyebrow rules, and the primary brand colour in dark mode (where the deep teal would disappear).





ZALF Green (#46A84F): The parent institution’s green; the growth note in the family.
Sage Light (#9EBC83): A soft light green used for headings and link/hover accents in dark mode, where it reads warmly against the near-black.
Misty Teal-Green (#80BDBD): The lightest teal; informational accents and tertiary tinting.




The three service pillars, each owning one colour. This triad is structural: it maps service → logo layer → colour, and appears on the concept diagram, the team-card top border, and the tiered service panels. - Surface Forest (#2B5D45) — Support, the surface stratum (logo layer 1). - Integration Terracotta (#A4713D) — Integration, the deep stratum (logo layer 3). The single warm earth tone, and the only non-green in the system. - Transfer Teal (#3E7775) — Transfer, the mid stratum (logo layer 2).




Warm Paper (#F5F3EE): The light-mode body background. Not white — a warm off-white that softens the whole system. The single most identity-defining neutral.
Slate (#465555): Default body text in light mode. A green-tinted dark grey, never pure black, so it sits in the family rather than fighting it.
Ink (#1A1A1A): Reserved near-black for the heaviest text.
Forest Ink (#0F1B18): The dark-mode body background — a teal-tinted near-black, deliberately richer than flat black.
Dark Surface (#162520) / Dark Border (#1F3530): Card surfaces and borders in dark mode.
Muted Gray (#6C6C6C): Captions, dates, and metadata. (In running text, body uses Slate at full strength, not this gray — see the Legibility Rule.)
Pure White (#FFFFFF): Card and surface fills that sit on top of the paper.





Olive (#B1BE4D): Warnings only.
Brick (#C0392B, #E74C3C dark): Danger / errors only.




The Strata Rule. Support is forest, Integration is terracotta, Transfer is teal — always, everywhere, in that mapping. The triad is never reassigned for visual variety and never used decoratively; if one of these colours appears, it means its pillar.
The One Earth Tone Rule. Terracotta is the only warm non-green in the system, and it belongs to Integration. Its rarity is what makes it legible. Do not introduce a second accent earth tone “for balance.”
The Legibility Rule. Body copy is Slate (#465555) on paper, never the muted gray. Gray (#6C6C6C) is for metadata only. Light-gray body text “for elegance” is forbidden — it fails our 4.5:1 floor and reads as the institutional cold we reject.

title: Design System: Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs (DML)
text:
Display Font: DM Serif Display (with Georgia, Times New Roman fallback) Body Font: DM Sans (with Segoe UI, system-ui fallback) Label/Mono Font: Segoe UI Mono (with ui-monospace, Consolas fallback)
Character: An editorial serif display paired with a clean geometric sans — a deliberate contrast-axis pairing (serif + sans), not two competing sans-serifs. The serif lends academic, considered weight to headings; the sans keeps the body readable and carries the warmth and approachability through running text. DM Serif Display ships in a single weight (400), so heading hierarchy is built from size and colour, not weight.

Identity note: DM Serif Display and DM Sans are on the greenfield reflex-reject list, but they are the brand’s committed, shipped typefaces — identity-preservation wins. Do not swap them on this surface.




Display (400, clamp(2.1rem, 5.5vw, 3.75rem), line-height 1.13, letter-spacing −0.01em): Hero headline only. Sentence case, balanced wrap. Tight, refined tracking — never wide or uppercased.
Headline (400, clamp(1.75rem, 3vw, 2.35rem), line-height 1.08): Major section titles (e.g. the support-tiers heading). Serif, teal-dark in light mode.
Title (400, 1.45rem, line-height 1.18, −0.01em): Card titles — team names, panel taglines. Serif, balanced wrap.
Body (400, 1rem, line-height 1.65): Running text in DM Sans. Generous leading. Cap measure at ~64ch (the components already constrain intros to 64ch / hero copy to 56ch).
Label (700, 0.68rem, letter-spacing 0.15em, UPPERCASE): Section eyebrows, column labels, the hero eyebrow, skill/role kickers. DM Sans, tracked, muted gray or tier colour. Short phrases only (≤4 words).
Mono (400, 0.9em): Inline code and kbd, on a paper-tinted (#EAE6DF) or dark-surface background.




The Serif-for-Voice, Sans-for-Cards Rule. Page and section headings are serif (editorial weight). But card titles in listings (news, projects) deliberately switch to DM Sans semibold near-black — the serif is reserved for identity moments, not every repeated grid title. Team-member names keep the serif because a person is an identity moment; a news headline is information.
The No-Weight-Crutch Rule. DM Serif Display has one weight. Build heading emphasis from size and colour, never from a bold that doesn’t exist. Never fake it with font-weight on the serif.

title: Design System: Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs (DML)
text:
The system is softly layered, not flat. Surfaces (cards, panels, the navbar) carry a quiet resting shadow and lift toward you on hover (translateY(-3px) to -4px) with a deeper shadow. The signature detail: shadows are tinted toward Forest Ink (rgba(15, 27, 24, …)), not pure black, so depth stays inside the warm palette instead of muddying it. The navbar uses a light glass treatment — backdrop-filter: blur(12px) over rgba(255,255,255,0.95) — the one place a blur is intentional rather than decorative.



Resting card (box-shadow: 0 12px 30px rgba(15,27,24,0.08), 0 3px 8px rgba(15,27,24,0.04)): The default lift for team cards and panels. Two layers: a soft ambient spread plus a tight contact shadow.
Hover card (box-shadow: 0 18px 36px rgba(15,27,24,0.12), 0 6px 14px rgba(15,27,24,0.06)): The lifted state, paired with translateY(-4px).
Listing hover (box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.09), 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.05)): Lighter cards (news/projects) rise on hover from a flat resting state.
Button (resting 0 2px 8px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); hover 0 4px 14px rgb(53 98 89 / 0.25)): The hover shadow tints toward teal-dark, glowing in the brand colour.
Floating panel (0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.1), 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.05)): Dropdown menus and the concept-diagram panels.




The Ink-Not-Black Rule. Shadows on light surfaces tint toward Forest Ink (rgba(15, 27, 24, …)), never rgba(0,0,0,…) at full neutrality. The warmth of the paper must survive into its shadows.
The Lift-on-Intent Rule. Surfaces rest quietly and lift only in response to the user (hover, focus). Elevation is feedback, not decoration. (Reduced-motion users get the colour/shadow change without the translate — see Do’s.)

title: Design System: Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs (DML)
text:
Shape: Gently rounded rectangles (8px / 0.5rem radius) — deliberately not pills (the brand moved off the 9999px pill).
Primary (.btn-brand): Deep Stratum Teal fill, white text, 600 weight, 0.65rem 1.5rem padding, a 1.5px teal border, and a soft resting shadow. Hover deepens the fill to #2A4E47 and lifts the shadow into a teal glow.
Hero / ghost (.hero-btn): On the dark hero, the same shape goes transparent with a rgba(255,255,255,0.4) border and near-white text; hover fills with rgba(255,255,255,0.1) and brightens the border. No shadow.
Button row: Buttons centre, wrap, and cap at 260px; on mobile they stack full-width.





Skill chip (.listing-skill): Pill-rounded (1rem), teal-tinted fill (rgba(teal-dark, 0.06)) with a faint teal border, teal-dark 700-weight UPPERCASE micro-label. Static (not interactive).
Project link (.project-link): 8px-rounded teal-tinted chip, semibold, deepens its tint on hover.
Category badge (.listing-category): Small 4px-rounded teal-tinted tag, 600-weight UPPERCASE, on news/project cards. Non-interactive (cursor: default).





Corner Style: Team cards 16px (1rem); listing cards 8px; signature panels 10–18px.
Team card (.card-team): White (or dark-surface) fill with a subtle top-light gradient overlay, a 4px strata-gradient top border (Support → Integration → Transfer), a circular 150px avatar inside a teal ring, serif name, tracked role kicker, skill chips, and a divider’d projects list. Lifts -4px on hover.
Listing card (news/projects): White, 8px, thin border, lifts -3px on hover. Internally reordered with flex order so meta reads: category → title → description → date.
Internal padding: Cards 1.5–1.75rem; signature panels clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 1.5rem).




The site is contact-driven, so forms are minimal — the navbar search is the main field. Inputs inherit Bootstrap/Quarto defaults, restyled to the palette: teal-dark icon glyphs, transparent backgrounds in the navbar, and a teal :focus-visible outline (2px solid, 2px offset). Any new field should follow the same pattern: light stroke, paper/white fill, teal focus ring — never a heavy box.




Navbar: Light glass — rgba(255,255,255,0.95) + blur(12px), a 1px hairline bottom border, dark glass (rgba(15,27,24,0.95)) in dark mode. Links are DM Sans 500, #4E5855, with a 4px-rounded teal-tint hover pill; active links go teal-dark 600 (sage-light in dark mode).
Language switcher: A bespoke inline EN / DE toggle (not a dropdown), the current language underlined in teal-dark, the other muted gray with a slash separator. Pinned to the navbar’s right edge on desktop.
Mobile: Collapses to a teal-stroked hamburger; nav items stack in-flow.




.col-section-label / divided-column h2: DM Sans, 0.68rem, 700, 0.15em tracking, UPPERCASE, muted gray, with a 1px rule that extends to fill the row (&::after { flex: 1; height: 1px }). This is the one deliberate, named eyebrow system — used for “NEWS”, “PROJECTS” column heads, not stamped above every section.



An interactive, paper-framed diagram (aspect-ratio: 1100/720) showing the three pillars orbiting a central “DML” label. Hovering/activating a stratum opens a white panel (badge in the tier colour, serif tagline, dotted list) with a soft fade-in. The visual argument for the whole service model — it shows the strata instead of listing them.



A three-step escalating ladder (.dml-support-tiers): three stepped panels of increasing height (12.75 → 15.75 → 18.5rem) in tier-tinted fills with a 6px coloured bottom border, effort “pips”, and an expanding detail panel. Lives in a paper-gradient, 18px-rounded, soft-shadowed container. Steps lift -4px and show a teal focus outline on keyboard focus.

title: Design System: Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs (DML)
text:
Do keep the Strata Rule absolute: Support = Surface Forest (#2B5D45), Integration = Integration Terracotta (#A4713D), Transfer = Transfer Teal (#3E7775), in that mapping, everywhere.
Do pair every tier colour with a label, icon, or position — colour-blind safe is non-negotiable. The strata triad must never carry meaning by colour alone.
Do set body copy in Slate (#465555) on paper at full strength; reserve muted gray (#6C6C6C) for dates and captions only. Verify ≥4.5:1 in both themes.
Do build heading hierarchy from size and colour — DM Serif Display has one weight (400).
Do tint shadows toward Forest Ink (rgba(15, 27, 24, …)), not pure black, on light surfaces.
Do give every hover/entrance animation a prefers-reduced-motion alternative: keep the colour and shadow change, drop the translateY.
Do keep the warm paper (#F5F3EE) as the light body and Forest Ink (#0F1B18) as the dark body — these define the brand more than any accent.
Do let the signature components (concept diagram, support tiers) carry structural meaning instead of writing another paragraph.





Don’t make it look like a generic SaaS landing page: no hero-metric template (big number / small label / gradient accent), no rows of identical icon-heading-text cards, no buzzwords (streamline, empower, supercharge, leverage, seamless, world-class).
Don’t make it look like a flashy startup: no dark-mode purple gradients, no neon accents, no glassmorphism as decoration. The one navbar blur is functional; do not multiply it.
Don’t make it look like a sterile government / institutional portal: never trade the warm paper and editorial serif for cold, template-stamped white.
Don’t make it read like a dense academic journal: never ship a wall of undifferentiated text — structure with hierarchy, whitespace, and the signature components.
Don’t use background-clip: text gradient text — emphasis is weight, size, or a single solid colour.
Don’t add a coloured border-left / border-right greater than 1px as a side stripe on cards or callouts. (The team-card top gradient and the tier bottom border are intentional top/bottom accents — the banned pattern is the side stripe.)
Don’t introduce a second warm/earth accent — terracotta is the only non-green, and it belongs to Integration.
Don’t stamp the tracked uppercase eyebrow above every section. It is one named system for column labels, not a per-section reflex.
Don’t revert buttons to pills — the brand uses 8px rounded rectangles.
Don’t use light-gray body text “for elegance”; it fails contrast and reads as the institutional cold the brand rejects.

text: In March 2026 the Innovation Center for Agricultural System Transformation (IAT) was officially launched, with two days of events at the Futurium in Berlin as well as the ZALF campus in Müncheberg. We were fortunate to have an opportunity to present our concept for how the Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs group (DML) will provide a three pillar approach of services to support IAT researchers and living labs in their data and modelling needs. title: Product
text:
brand



Researchers, PhD candidates, and project partners inside the Innovation Center for Agricultural System Transformation (IAT) at the Leibniz Centre for Agricultural Landscape Research (ZALF), plus external collaborators in agricultural Living Lab projects.
They arrive with a concrete need — “I have data/models and don’t know how to manage, connect, or hand them off” — and a limited tolerance for jargon. Most are domain scientists (agronomy, soil, landscape, environmental modelling), not data engineers. They visit to understand what the working group offers, see whether it fits their project, and find the right person to talk to. The conversion action is almost always starting a conversation (email, a meeting), not a self-serve signup.



The public site of the Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs (DML) working group. It exists to:

Explain the group’s three-pillar service model — Support (managing research data and software across the full scientific life cycle), Integration (connecting data and methods across IAT research groups), and Transfer (closing the loop between science and practice).
Make the group legible and approachable so a researcher can self-identify their need and reach out.
Showcase people, projects, and news that build trust in the group’s competence.

Success looks like a researcher landing on the site, recognising their problem in one of the three pillars, and contacting the team — without first having to decode institutional language.



Warm, collaborative, approachable.
This is a service group, not a gatekeeping authority. The voice is that of a knowledgeable colleague who is glad you asked, not a faceless institution. Scientific credibility is the baseline (it is a ZALF/Leibniz research unit and must read as competent and trustworthy), but warmth and accessibility are what differentiate it: the design should feel human and inviting, lowering the barrier to “discuss your project with us.” Clear language over institutional jargon. Care over polish-for-its-own-sake.



The site should explicitly not look or feel like any of these:

A generic SaaS landing page — no hero-metric template (big number / small label / gradient accent), no endless rows of identical icon-heading-text cards, no marketing buzzwords (streamline, empower, supercharge, leverage, seamless, world-class).
A flashy startup — no dark-mode purple gradients, neon accents, or glassmorphism-as-decoration. (The site has a genuine dark mode and one subtle navbar blur; those are functional, not the aesthetic.)
A sterile government / institutional portal — not cold, bureaucratic, or template-stamped. The warmth of the paper background and editorial type is the antidote.
A dense academic journal — not a wall of undifferentiated text. Hierarchy, whitespace, and visual structure (the concept diagram, the tiered service panels) carry the meaning.





Practice what you preach. A data-and-modelling group’s own site should itself be well-structured, accessible, and FAIR-minded. Craft is evidence of competence.
Service, not gatekeeping. Every screen should lower the barrier to making contact. Warmth and clarity over institutional distance.
Show the structure. The three-pillar (Support / Integration / Transfer) strata model is the core idea — make it visible and walkable, not buried in prose.
Clarity over jargon. Approachable language a domain scientist understands beats precise-but-opaque institutional wording.
Trust through care, not noise. Credibility comes from restraint, legibility, and attention to detail — never from louder visuals.




Target WCAG 2.1 AA as the floor, consistent with EU public-sector obligations (BITV 2.0 / EN 301 549) for a ZALF/Leibniz site.

Body text contrast ≥ 4.5:1; large text ≥ 3:1, in both light and dark themes.
Honour prefers-reduced-motion: every entrance/hover animation needs a reduced or instant alternative.
Colour-blind safe: the Support / Integration / Transfer triad must never carry meaning by colour alone — always pair with a label, icon, or position.
Full keyboard operability and visible focus states (the design already uses :focus-visible outlines on interactive elements).
Respect the user’s OS colour-scheme preference (respect-user-color-scheme).

title: MonksHillLabs Initiative
text:
MonksHillLabs is a collaborative research platform that provides shared computational infrastructure, data repositories, and development environments for landscape and land use modelling projects.
The initiative brings together researchers, data scientists, and software developers to co-create tools, standards, and workflows that advance data interoperability and reproducible research in landscape science.
Current activities include developing standardized data formats, building modular modelling components, and hosting hackathons and training workshops.

title: Datenschutzerklärung
text:
1. Zweck dieser Datenschutzerklärung
Die Arbeitsgruppe „Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs (DML)“ am Leibniz-Zentrum für Agrarlandschaftsforschung (ZALF) legt großen Wert auf den Schutz Ihrer personenbezogenen Daten. Diese Datenschutzerklärung informiert darüber, welche personenbezogenen Daten beim Besuch dieser Website verarbeitet werden können, zu welchen Zwecken dies geschieht und welche Rechte Ihnen zustehen.

title: Datenschutzerklärung
text:
2. Erhebung und Verarbeitung von Daten
Da es sich um eine statische Website auf GitHub Pages handelt, verarbeiten wir selbst keine personenbezogenen Daten aktiv. Im Rahmen des Betriebs können jedoch durch den Hosting-Anbieter folgende Daten verarbeitet werden:

Protokolldaten: Informationen wie IP-Adresse, Browsertyp, Betriebssystem, Referrer-URL, aufgerufene Seiten und Zeitstempel können von GitHub Pages protokolliert werden.
Cookies: Diese Website setzt selbst keine Tracking-Cookies. GitHub kann Cookies einsetzen, um seine Dienste bereitzustellen und abzusichern.

Weitere Informationen finden Sie in der GitHub-Datenschutzerklärung.

title: Datenschutzerklärung
text:
3. Zweck der Verarbeitung
Wir verwenden personenbezogene Daten nicht für Analyse-, Marketing- oder Profiling-Zwecke. Eine etwaige Verarbeitung durch GitHub (z. B. Server-Logs) dient dem Betrieb und der Sicherheit der Hosting-Plattform.

title: Datenschutzerklärung
text:
4. Weitergabe von Daten
Wir verkaufen oder vermieten keine personenbezogenen Daten und geben sie nicht an Dritte weiter. GitHub kann Daten als Hosting-Anbieter gemäß seiner Datenschutzerklärung verarbeiten.

title: Datenschutzerklärung
text:
5. Rechte der betroffenen Personen (DSGVO)
Nach der DSGVO haben Sie insbesondere folgende Rechte:

Auskunft (Art. 15)
Berichtigung (Art. 16)
Löschung (Art. 17)
Einschränkung der Verarbeitung (Art. 18)
Widerspruch (Art. 21)
Datenübertragbarkeit (Art. 20)

Zudem haben Sie das Recht, sich bei einer Aufsichtsbehörde zu beschweren (Art. 77).

title: Datenschutzerklärung
text:
6. Speicherdauer
Wir speichern über diese Website keine personenbezogenen Daten. Etwaige Protokolldaten werden durch GitHub gemäß deren Aufbewahrungsrichtlinien verarbeitet.

title: Datenschutzerklärung
text:
7. Dienste Dritter und externe Links
Diese Website kann Links zu externen Websites enthalten. Für deren Datenschutzpraktiken sind wir nicht verantwortlich. Bitte beachten Sie die jeweiligen Datenschutzhinweise.

title: Datenschutzerklärung
text:
8. Sicherheitsmaßnahmen
Diese Website betreibt keine eigene Nutzerdatenbank. GitHub Pages stellt Betriebs- und Plattform-Sicherheit bereit. Weitere Informationen finden Sie in GitHub’s Security overview.

Wir können diese Datenschutzerklärung anpassen, um rechtliche Anforderungen oder Änderungen der Website abzubilden. Die jeweils aktuelle Version wird auf dieser Seite veröffentlicht.
